title: Angles in Parallel Lines & Polygons
description: Angles on parallel lines, interior and exterior angles of polygons.

notes.heading: Parallel Lines and Transversals

illustration.alt: Diagram of two parallel lines crossed by a transversal, showing corresponding, alternate and co-interior angles, plus a hexagon with interior and exterior angles marked.
illustration.caption: Parallel lines and a transversal create three special angle pairs: corresponding (a), alternate (b) and co-interior (c). Polygons have interior angles (x) and exterior angles (y).

notes.body:
📌 Definition
Parallel lines are straight lines in the same plane that never meet. A transversal is a straight line that crosses two or more parallel lines.

🔑 Key Concept
When a transversal crosses parallel lines, three important angle pairs are formed:
• Corresponding angles: equal (they make an F shape).
• Alternate angles: equal (they make a Z shape).
• Co-interior angles: add to $180^{\circ}$ (they make a C shape).

💡 Worked Example
Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. One corresponding angle is $62^{\circ}$. Find the co-interior angle on the same side.

Step 1: The corresponding angle is $62^{\circ}$, so the angle in the same position on the other parallel line is also $62^{\circ}$.

Step 2: Co-interior angles add to $180^{\circ}$.
$$180^{\circ} - 62^{\circ} = 118^{\circ}$$

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Only use these rules when the lines are parallel.
• Look for the F, Z and C shapes to identify angle pairs quickly.
• Always write a reason for each step in an angle problem.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Assuming lines are parallel without checking for arrow marks or being told so.

notes.heading: Corresponding and Alternate Angles
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Corresponding angles are in matching positions at each intersection where the transversal crosses the parallel lines. Alternate angles are between the parallel lines on opposite sides of the transversal.

🔑 Key Concept
When lines are parallel:
$$\text{corresponding angle} = \text{corresponding angle}$$
$$\text{alternate angle} = \text{alternate angle}$$

💡 Worked Example
Find angle $x$ when a transversal makes an angle of $55^{\circ}$ with one of two parallel lines and $x$ is alternate to it.

Because alternate angles are equal:
$$x = 55^{\circ}$$

✅ Check
The two angles form a Z shape and are on opposite sides of the transversal.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Corresponding angles make an F shape.
• Alternate angles make a Z shape.
• Vertically opposite angles at each intersection are also equal.

notes.heading: Co-Interior Angles
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Co-interior angles are the angles that lie between the parallel lines and on the same side of the transversal.

🔑 Key Concept
Co-interior angles are supplementary, which means they add to $180^{\circ}$.
$$a + b = 180^{\circ}$$

💡 Worked Example
Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. One co-interior angle is $72^{\circ}$. Find the other.

$$180^{\circ} - 72^{\circ} = 108^{\circ}$$

The other co-interior angle is $108^{\circ}$.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Thinking co-interior angles are equal. They are supplementary, not equal.

✅ Check
$72^{\circ} + 108^{\circ} = 180^{\circ}$.

notes.heading: Interior Angle Sum of a Polygon
notes.body:
📌 Definition
The interior angles of a polygon are the angles inside the shape at each vertex.

🔑 Key Concept
A polygon with $n$ sides can be split into $(n - 2)$ triangles. Since the angles in every triangle add to $180^{\circ}$:
$$\text{sum of interior angles} = (n - 2) \times 180^{\circ}$$

💡 Worked Example
Find the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon. A hexagon has $n = 6$.

$$(6 - 2) \times 180^{\circ} = 4 \times 180^{\circ} = 720^{\circ}$$

📎 Key Points to Remember
• The formula works for any polygon.
• A triangle has $n = 3$: $(3 - 2) \times 180^{\circ} = 180^{\circ}$.
• A quadrilateral has $n = 4$: $(4 - 2) \times 180^{\circ} = 360^{\circ}$.

notes.heading: Exterior Angle Sum of a Polygon
notes.body:
📌 Definition
An exterior angle is formed by extending one side of a polygon at a vertex. At each vertex, one interior angle and one exterior angle sit on a straight line.

🔑 Key Concept
For any polygon, the sum of the exterior angles, taking one at each vertex, is always $360^{\circ}$. This is true no matter how many sides the polygon has.
$$\text{sum of exterior angles} = 360^{\circ}$$

💡 Worked Example
A pentagon has exterior angles $70^{\circ}$, $80^{\circ}$, $90^{\circ}$, $65^{\circ}$ and $x$. Find $x$.

$$70^{\circ} + 80^{\circ} + 90^{\circ} + 65^{\circ} + x = 360^{\circ}$$
$$305^{\circ} + x = 360^{\circ}$$
$$x = 55^{\circ}$$

✅ Check
The five exterior angles add to $360^{\circ}$.

notes.heading: Regular Polygons
notes.body:
📌 Definition
A regular polygon has all sides equal and all angles equal.

🔑 Key Concept
For a regular polygon with $n$ sides:
$$\text{one exterior angle} = \dfrac{360^{\circ}}{n}$$
$$\text{one interior angle} = \dfrac{(n - 2) \times 180^{\circ}}{n}$$

Also, at each vertex:
$$\text{interior angle} + \text{exterior angle} = 180^{\circ}$$

💡 Worked Example
Find the interior and exterior angles of a regular octagon ($n = 8$).

Exterior angle:
$$\dfrac{360^{\circ}}{8} = 45^{\circ}$$

Interior angle:
$$180^{\circ} - 45^{\circ} = 135^{\circ}$$

✅ Check
$135^{\circ} + 45^{\circ} = 180^{\circ}$.

notes.heading: Multi-step Angle Problems
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Many angle problems need more than one angle fact used in a sequence.

🔑 How it works
1. Mark every angle you know on the diagram.
2. Use parallel-line facts for corresponding, alternate or co-interior angles.
3. Use triangle, quadrilateral or polygon angle sums when shapes are involved.
4. Write a reason next to each step.

💡 Worked Example
Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. One angle is $48^{\circ}$. Find the angle $x$ that is co-interior to the vertically opposite angle of $48^{\circ}$.

Step 1: The angle vertically opposite $48^{\circ}$ is also $48^{\circ}$.

Step 2: The co-interior angle adds to $180^{\circ}$.
$$x = 180^{\circ} - 48^{\circ} = 132^{\circ}$$

⚠️ Common Mistake
Missing a step or using the wrong angle pair. Always identify parallel lines, transversals and shapes first.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Angles on a straight line add to $180^{\circ}$.
• Angles around a point add to $360^{\circ}$.
• Vertically opposite angles are equal.

flashcards.definition: A straight line that crosses two or more other lines.
flashcards.example: A transversal crossing two parallel lines creates eight angles.

flashcards.definition: Equal angles in matching positions when a transversal crosses parallel lines.
flashcards.example: If one corresponding angle is $62^{\circ}$, the other is also $62^{\circ}$.

flashcards.definition: Equal angles between parallel lines on opposite sides of a transversal.
flashcards.example: Alternate angles of $55^{\circ}$ and $55^{\circ}$ form a Z shape.

flashcards.definition: Angles between parallel lines on the same side of a transversal; they are supplementary.
The sum of the interior angles of a polygon with $n$ sides.
The sum of one exterior angle at each vertex of any polygon.
flashcards.example: For every polygon the exterior angles add to $360^{\circ}$.

flashcards.definition: A polygon with all sides equal and all angles equal.
flashcards.example: A regular hexagon has six equal sides and six equal angles.

flashcards.term: Interior angle of a regular polygon
flashcards.definition: One interior angle of a regular polygon with $n$ sides.

flashcards.term: Exterior angle of a regular polygon
flashcards.definition: One exterior angle of a regular polygon with $n$ sides.

flashcards.term: Number of sides from an exterior angle
flashcards.definition: A way to find how many sides a regular polygon has from one exterior angle.
flashcards.example: $n = \dfrac{360^{\circ}}{\text{one exterior angle}}$. An exterior angle of $30^{\circ}$ means $12$ sides.

flashcards.definition: At any vertex of a polygon, the interior angle and exterior angle add to $180^{\circ}$.
flashcards.example: If the interior angle is $150^{\circ}$, the exterior angle is $30^{\circ}$.

flashcards.definition: The three angle-pair rules used when a transversal crosses parallel lines.
flashcards.example: Corresponding angles are equal, alternate angles are equal and co-interior angles add to $180^{\circ}$.

questions.stem: Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. One corresponding angle is $58^{\circ}$. What is the other corresponding angle?
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles are equal when lines are parallel, so the other corresponding angle is also $58^{\circ}$.

questions.stem: Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. One alternate angle is $47^{\circ}$. What is the other alternate angle?
questions.explanation: Alternate angles are equal when lines are parallel, so the other alternate angle is also $47^{\circ}$.

questions.stem: Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. One co-interior angle is $65^{\circ}$. What is the other co-interior angle?
questions.explanation: Co-interior angles add to $180^{\circ}$, so the missing angle is $180^{\circ} - 65^{\circ} = 115^{\circ}$.

questions.stem: Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. One angle is $55^{\circ}$. What is the corresponding angle?
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles are equal, so the corresponding angle is $55^{\circ}$.

questions.stem: Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. One angle is $112^{\circ}$. What is the alternate angle?
questions.explanation: Alternate angles are equal, so the alternate angle is $112^{\circ}$.

questions.stem: Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. One angle is $38^{\circ}$. What is the co-interior angle on the same side?
questions.explanation: Co-interior angles add to $180^{\circ}$, so the missing angle is $180^{\circ} - 38^{\circ} = 142^{\circ}$.

questions.stem: What is the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon?
What is the sum of the interior angles of an octagon?
What is the size of one exterior angle of a regular pentagon?
questions.explanation: For a regular polygon, one exterior angle is $\dfrac{360^{\circ}}{n}$. With $n = 5$, this is $\dfrac{360^{\circ}}{5} = 72^{\circ}$.

questions.stem: A regular polygon has an exterior angle of $24^{\circ}$. How many sides does it have?
questions.explanation: The number of sides is $n = \dfrac{360^{\circ}}{\text{exterior angle}} = \dfrac{360^{\circ}}{24^{\circ}} = 15$.

questions.stem: What is the size of one interior angle of a regular hexagon?
A regular polygon has an interior angle of $150^{\circ}$. What is the exterior angle?
questions.explanation: Interior and exterior angles add to $180^{\circ}$, so the exterior angle is $180^{\circ} - 150^{\circ} = 30^{\circ}$.

questions.stem: A regular polygon has an interior angle of $150^{\circ}$. How many sides does it have?
The exterior angles of a hexagon are $60^{\circ}$, $70^{\circ}$, $80^{\circ}$, $55^{\circ}$, $50^{\circ}$ and $x$. Find $x$.
questions.explanation: The sum of exterior angles is $360^{\circ}$. So $x = 360^{\circ} - 60^{\circ} - 70^{\circ} - 80^{\circ} - 55^{\circ} - 50^{\circ} = 45^{\circ}$.

questions.stem: Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. One angle is $70^{\circ}$. Find the angle that is co-interior to the vertically opposite angle of $70^{\circ}$.
questions.explanation: The vertically opposite angle is also $70^{\circ}$. The co-interior angle adds to $180^{\circ}$, so it is $180^{\circ} - 70^{\circ} = 110^{\circ}$.
